items.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24
items.q: But when I was a little girl, about ten years old, Tim, we lived in the country and I came here.

ctx.x: That's all, that's all, that's out from Tibidon. A mile and a half? Yeah. That's a, for instance, you cross the U.P. Long Bridge, you know. Oh yeah. And get that, keep you all the way going to Tibidon. And you wouldn't turn left, continue right. On the bayou.

Yeah, on the bayou. On the bayou. On that bayou. Bayou Lafour. On that road. On that road. Continue on that bayou Lafour. A mile and a half from Donisonville. Donisonville. On bayou Lafour. And you can't miss it because that great big Catholic church is there. Noted, oh, it's been there over a hundred years. Since, what, St. uh, the Ascension. The Ascension. The Ascension. The Catholic church. There where I was christened there. And, uh, made my communion there. That big church. And in those days, now, I don't…
